requirements.title: A unit specified by an io-unit refers to a file
requirements.definition: A unit, specified by an io-unit, provides a means for referring to a file.

pending.io-unit-refers-to-file: Use a future internal-file and external-file data-transfer pair with variables initialized to nondefault sentinels; assert that each io-unit selects the intended file effect, not a processor-dependent numeric unit.

requirements.oracle: Plans are pending and source-derived. Positive plans establish a non-default state first (for example by writing known records, initializing variables to nonzero/nonblank sentinels, or creating a known file) and then observe only portable properties: exact internal records, successful IOSTAT zero, nonzero IOSTAT for a specified error condition, or named intrinsic status values where the standard names them. Processor-dependent unit numbers, file names, record lengths, storage-unit encodings, buffering, timing, IOMSG text, and specific error numbers are not asserted.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Source accounting only. requirements.title: An io-unit is a file-unit-number, an asterisk, or an internal-file-variable
requirements.definition: The io-unit syntax admits exactly a file-unit-number, an asterisk, or an internal-file-variable.

pending.io-unit-file-unit-number-form: Compile a complete READ or WRITE using an established scalar integer file-unit-number in a valid I/O control; repair negatives change only the io-unit token to an unadmitted form.
pending.io-unit-asterisk-form: Compile complete READ(*,...) and WRITE(*,...) controls with no claim about the external medium; repair a negative by restoring the asterisk in the io-unit slot only.
pending.io-unit-internal-file-variable-form: Compile an internal READ/WRITE using a default-character variable initialized to nonblank sentinel content; repair negatives change only the io-unit to the character variable.

requirements.title: Units are external or internal and their designators determine the file category
requirements.definition: A unit is either external or internal. An external unit refers to an external file and is specified by an asterisk or file-unit-number. An internal unit refers to an internal file and is specified by an internal-file-variable or by a defined-I/O unit argument value.

pending.external-unit-designates-external-file: Create or use a known external connection and read/write known records; assert the data effect through the external unit, not the numeric unit value or path representation.
pending.internal-unit-designates-internal-file: Use a CHARACTER variable internal file with nonblank sentinel contents and exact internal READ/WRITE observations; do not infer external connection state.

requirements.title: A file-unit-number value shall identify a valid unit from the permitted value set
requirements.definition: A file-unit-number value shall be nonnegative, an active defined-I/O unit argument, a NEWUNIT value, or one of INPUT_UNIT, OUTPUT_UNIT, or ERROR_UNIT; the value shall identify a valid unit.

pending.file-unit-number-valid-unit: Establish validity first by OPEN(NEWUNIT=...) or a named preconnected constant, then perform a known I/O operation; do not rely on a guessed small integer or on IOMSG text.

pending.read-without-control-list-uses-input-uni: Use READ x with controlled stdin and a nondefault sentinel; assert the input value is assigned, not any prompt or terminal behavior.

pending.error-unit-error_unit-constant: Use the named constant directly and never assert its numeric value; data effect is observed through a distinctive output record.

Input and output preconnected-unit rules are split by role and named constant.
READ asterisk identifies the input unit.

READ without control list uses input unit.
WRITE asterisk identifies output unit.
Output unit preconnection obligation.

PRINT uses output unit.
Mixed error-unit obligation and processor latitude are split.

review_rationale: Source registration for 12.5-12.5.5, units and their connection to files (batch150). Every unit hash-verified against the pinned census by an independent reviewer across two rounds. Round 1 found an over-suppressed facet - that an unformatted connection has no changeable modes IS portably observable through INQUIRE returning UNDEFINED for BLANK=, DECIMAL=, DELIM=, LEADING_ZERO=, PAD=, ROUND= and SIGN= - and a conditional C1202 negative, now recorded as source-only because no character kind beyond default, ASCII and ISO 10646 is guaranteed. The five numbered rules R1201-R1203, C1201 and C1202 were pre-accounted. Source accounting only.
